scenarios.query:
Audit this decision-record scan:
```text
id      status    supersedes  technology  revisit_trigger  last_touched  notes
ADR-8   accepted  -           Kafka       -                2 years ago   "event bus, subsystem: orders"
ADR-14  accepted  -           SQS         -                3 months ago  "event bus, subsystem: orders"
```
expected_behavior: Flags the status-graph contradiction: both ADR-8 (Kafka) and ADR-14 (SQS) are accepted for the same subsystem (orders event bus) with no supersedes/superseded-by link between them
Recommends marking one as superseded or recording why both stand
Does not attempt to judge which technology choice is correct — only that the record graph is inconsistent

scenarios.query:
Audit this decision-record scan (archive index lists ADR-1 through ADR-9; the directory on disk also contains `ADR-9-b-cache-invalidation.md`, not listed in the index; two separate files on disk are both titled `ADR-9` — `ADR-9-varnish-edge-cache.md` and `ADR-9-log-retention.md`):
```text
id      status    supersedes  technology  revisit_trigger  last_touched  notes
ADR-9   accepted  -           Varnish     -                1 year ago    "edge cache (ADR-9-varnish-edge-cache.md)"
ADR-9   accepted  -           -           -                6 months ago  "log retention policy (ADR-9-log-retention.md)"
```
expected_behavior: Flags the duplicate record ID: two distinct files on disk both use the identifier ADR-9 (edge-cache and log-retention) — a scan-reliability defect in its own right, separate from any content judgment about either record
Separately flags the archive's own index as out of date: a file on disk (`ADR-9-b-cache-invalidation.md`) is not listed in the index, so the sweep's own view of the archive may be incomplete
Surfaces both as scan-reliability signals, not decision-content findings about the records themselves
Routes the general index/discoverability upkeep to auditing-documentation-health (#22) rather than treating it as this lens's own content judgment
